items.title: Announcing Rust 1.100.0
items.summary: release, rust
items.content:
The Rust team is happy to announce a new version of Rust, 1.100.0. Rust is a programming language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.

If you have a previous version of Rust installed via rustup , you can get 1.100.0 with:

If you don't have it already, you can get rustup from the appropriate page on our website, and check out the detailed release notes for 1.100.0 .

If you'd like to help us out by testing future releases, you might consider updating locally to use the beta channel ( rustup default beta ) or the nightly channel ( rustup default nightly ). Please report any bugs you might come across!

After 10 years and 5 failed stabilization attempts, the never type is finally stable ! This also completes the project goal for this work.

The never type, spelled ! in code, is the canonical uninhabited type. It represents the type of diverging computations – computations which never resolve to any value – where any code that follows is unreachable. Expressions that terminate control flow, such as return , break , and std::process::exit , also have the type ! .

Since having a value of the never type is impossible, Rust permits a never-to-any coercion, allowing to turn ! into any other type (this is what distinguishes it from any other uninhabited types). This can be used, for example, to not return a value from one of the branches of a match or an if :

While the never type could already be used and observed this way, and even named in the return type of functions ( -> ! ), this release allows naming the never type anywhere:

Additionally this release changes Infallible to be an alias to the never type. That makes all old APIs that used Infallible be compatible with using ! . This was the plan ever since the introduction of Infallible and is one of the reasons why the never type stabilization was so hard (waffle gave a talk about some of the troubles of the stabilization).

Unfortunately, to allow changing Infallible , we had to introduce a breaking change. This release changes the "never type fallback" from () to ! in editions before 2024 (i.e. 2015, 2018, and 2021), similarly to what has already been done in edition 2024 . This should largely be unnoticeable, but can affect code in some rare cases (for example when ignoring a result of a function returning a generic parameter). Note that this change might also make the compiler detect more code as unreachable.

We tried to minimize the impact of this breaking change as much as possible, by providing future compatibility warnings far in advance and releasing fixes to public crates that have been broken by this. If a dependency is failing due to issues with the never type, consider updating it, as a fix might have already been released for it.

This release brings about the stabilization of the core parts of allocator_api , enabling library authors to define custom allocators that can be used together with certain standard library types - currently Vec and Box . These are enabled through the newly-stabilized Allocator trait.

This is the foundation of the Allocators 1.0 project goal . A lot remains to be done still, including expanding the API surface usable with custom allocators and stabilizing their use on more collections and pointer types; with the core trait and design out of the way though, expect to see more being stabilized soon!

The Drop trait in Rust makes it possible to run code when a variable goes out of scope, regardless of whether we return , ? , or panic. Drop being a part of types means that in Rust you never have to close a socket .

Implementing Drop can however feel a little inconvenient when all you want is to run some code unconditionally when a function exits. This is why we’re introducing core::mem::DropGuard : a new helper type that runs a closure when dropped.

items.title: Vivaldi CEO explains his anti-AI stance: most users don’t want AI in the browser
items.content:
Vivaldi’s CEO says most users do not want AI features built into their browser.

Vivaldi reports 50% to 100% user growth across many European countries.

The company says it does not collect user data and keeps data local or encrypted.

Tetzchner says Vivaldi prefers human engineers to write code instead of relying on AI.

Key Takeaways by nexos.ai , reviewed by Cybernews staff.

Jon von Tetzchner, CEO and founder of Vivaldi Technologies, refuses to integrate AI features in its browser and wants human engineers, not AI, to write its code.

I spoke to Tetzchner on the sidelines of the Web Summit in Lisbon, where we discussed an increasing interest in the privacy-focused Vivaldi browser amid growing disillusionment with the big tech and Europeans’ efforts to achieve digital sovereignty.

Tetzchner says in the last year, the number of Vivaldi users grew by between 50% and 100% across many European countries. The company also sees an increasing user base in Canada and the US.

Big tech isn’t safe anymore, and people are looking for alternatives, so they’re coming to us. I think people in the US are just as disgusted with big tech as just about everyone else,

Jon von Tetzchner, CEO and founder of Vivaldi Technologies, tells Cybernews.

Proton issues an apology, says its AI use will never come at the expense of security

Sovereign AI plan "makes no sense," German MP says

There’s no winner nor the finish line in the US-China AI race, an expert says

“Customer data leaked”: AI agents cause a security nightmare for companies

Chip export to China will continue despite Nvidia spying allegations, an expert says

OpenAI is racing to kill rogue AI in 35 seconds

Vivaldi is marketed as a privacy-focused browser that doesn’t collect user data, which is either stored locally on the user’s device or is encrypted.

It also stands out from its competitors by its strict anti-AI stance, as it refuses to embed AI features, such as auto-summary, in the browser.

Tetzchner says the company asked its users whether they wanted added AI features, and the response was “no.”

He argues that most Vivaldi’s competitors are developed by ad companies, which use AI features to collect user data. Meanwhile, competitors that previously added AI to their products now market themselves as AI-free.

“I think this means that users don't like to be told what to do. They want their own agency. They want to be able to do what they want with their browser without AI agents getting in the way of it,” he says.

Stay updated with our latest stories and follow us on social media

Be the first to discover new stories, ideas, and updates from our team.

Vivaldi integrates Proton VPN into its desktop browser. The Swiss company recently faced major public backlash after 404 Media reported that its CEO, Andy Yen, pressures engineers to use AI to write code, sparking security concerns among Proton users. Some swore they were canceling their Proton subscription .

Tetzchner told Cybernews that Proton is dealing with its AI-related issues, calling the situation “unfortunate.”

He claims that Vivaldi Technologies doesn’t actively use AI, and he would rather see its engineers write their own code.

“We don't want a situation where people are using AI to write code and don't understand what they've been doing,” he explains.

At the same time, the company has to address the cybersecurity risks posed by AI.

“It’s a brilliant business model to build a tool for hacking things, which makes everyone want to buy that tool so they could defend themselves,” Tetzchner says.

items.title: LG facing a lawsuit in Portugal for alleged “domestic espionage” through their TVs (article in Portuguese)
items.content:
O processo deu entrada no Tribunal Cível de Lisboa e envolve também dois dos maiores retalhistas de eletrónica em Portugal, a FNAC e a Worten.

A LG, gigante sul-coreana do setor da eletrónica, vai responder em tribunal na sequência de uma ação popular apresentada pela associação de defesa dos consumidores Citizens Voice, que acusa alguns modelos de televisores da marca de terem capacidades que poderão permitir a captação e gravação de áudio dentro das habitações, mesmo com o ecrã desligado. O processo deu entrada no Tribunal Cível de Lisboa e envolve também dois dos maiores retalhistas de eletrónica em Portugal, a FNAC e a Worten.

Segundo o Correio da Manhã (CM) , a associação pretende que a LG seja impedida de fabricar televisores com as características contestadas e que disponibilize a reparação gratuita dos aparelhos já vendidos aos consumidores que a solicitem. Em relação à FNAC e à Worten, o pedido passa por impedir a comercialização dos modelos identificados, alegadamente equipados com software capaz de captar comunicações. A Citizens Voice pede ainda a realização de uma perícia técnica aos televisores em causa, para apurar as capacidades efetivas dos equipamentos e esclarecer se existe recolha de áudio fora das situações em que o utilizador interage conscientemente com o aparelho.

A contestação surgiu na sequência de uma investigação divulgada em setembro pelo canal de YouTube Gamers Nexus, em colaboração com a Level1Techs. A análise identificou alguns submodelos da gama Smart TV OLED da LG que, segundo os investigadores, conseguiam analisar a rede local em busca de dispositivos sem relação direta com o televisor, como smartphones, e recolher dados técnicos, incluindo endereços IP, identificadores de redes Wi-Fi (SSID), intensidade do sinal de redes próximas e informação de localização geográfica. A investigação levantou também suspeitas sobre a possibilidade de captação e gravação de áudio com o ecrã desligado.

A LG rejeitou, na sequência da divulgação da investigação, que os seus televisores gravem conversas ambientes de forma indiscriminada. Num comunicado, a empresa afirmou que os dados de voz apenas são processados quando o utilizador prime o botão de voz e é reconhecida uma palavra de ativação. “Fora destas situações, as TV’s não recolhem nem gravam conversas e ambiente”, garantiu a marca. A Citizens Voice contesta esta explicação na ação judicial, alegando que a captação não se limita aos momentos em que o consumidor pretende dar um comando de voz. Na petição inicial, a associação sustenta que a investigação documenta capacidades de captação de áudio com o ecrã desligado, bem como gravação e conservação local em circunstâncias que não dependem de uma interação consciente do utilizador. Caberá agora ao processo judicial esclarecer os factos e avaliar os pedidos apresentados.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-126366 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False MessagePack for Ruby is an implementation of the MessagePack binary serialization format. Prior to 1.8.7, the Java-platform msgpack gem for JRuby allocated arrays and byte buffers directly from attacker-controlled array32, str32, and bin32 declared sizes before confirming that corresponding elements or bytes were available. A short MessagePack header could therefore trigger a very large allocation or sustained heap growth when an application decoded untrusted input through MessagePack.unpack or MessagePack::Unpacker, potentially exhausting the shared JVM heap. map32 and declared counts at or above 2^31 did not use the affected allocation behavior. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.7. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-12T22:41:38.409Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-126366
items.title_ko: CVE-2026-126366: MessagePack for Ruby JRuby 구현체의 과도한 메모리 할당 취약점
items.summary_ko: 1.8.7 이전 버전의 JRuby용 msgpack gem은 공격자가 선언한 크기만큼 배열과 버퍼를 확인 없이 할당했다. 짧은 헤더만으로도 대규모 메모리 할당이나 힙 증가가 발생해 JVM 힙이 고갈될 수 있다. 이 문제는 1.8.7에서 수정됐다.
items.content_ko: MessagePack for Ruby는 MessagePack 바이너리 직렬화 형식의 구현체다. 1.8.7 이전의 Java 플랫폼용 msgpack gem은 JRuby에서 사용될 때 array32, str32, bin32 헤더에 선언된 크기를 실제 데이터 존재 여부를 확인하기 전에 그대로 할당했다. 신뢰할 수 없는 입력을 MessagePack.unpack 또는 MessagePack::Unpacker로 디코딩하면 짧은 헤더만으로도 큰 메모리 할당이 발생하거나 힙이 계속 커질 수 있으며, 공유 JVM 힙이 고갈될 가능성이 있다. map32와 2^31 이상의 선언된 개수에서는 이 문제가 나타나지 않았다. 취약점은 1.8.7에서 수정됐다. 소스는 GitHub_M, CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 가능성은 False로 표기됐다. 공개일은 2026-11-12다.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: The entirety of "Let Over Lambda" is now freely available online
items.summary: book, lisp
items.content:
Let Over Lambda (ISBN 978-1-4357-1275-1, 376+iv pp.) is one of the most hardcore computer programming books out there. Starting with the fundamentals, it describes the most advanced features of the most advanced language: C OMMON L ISP . The point of this book is to expose you to ideas that you might otherwise never be exposed to.

This book is about macros, that is programs that write programs. Macros are what make lisp the greatest programming language in the world. When used properly, macros enable amazing feats of abstraction, programmer productivity, and code efficiency and security that are unheard of elsewhere. Macros let you do things you simply cannot do in other languages.

If you are looking for a dry coding manual that re-hashes common-sense techniques in whatever langue du jour, this book is not for you. This book is about pushing the boundaries of what we know about programming. While this book teaches useful macro skills that can help solve your programming problems today and now, it has also been designed to be entertaining and inspiring. If you have ever wondered what lisp or even programming itself is really about, this is the book you have been looking for.

2026 update: Let Over Lambda was published in 2008, to align with the 50th anniversary of Lisp's invention in 1958. A lot has changed since then, in both Lisp and programming practice in general. Although my thinking and opinions have evolved since, I still believe the book holds up well as a tutorial and explanation of why Lisp so special. Going forward, the entire book is free to read online ( HTML , PDF ). Happy lisping!

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Israel has a lot riding on Nvidia, whose CEO resigned today
items.content:
Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, during an October 2026 television interview in London. Photo by Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and has run it for 33 years, resigned as chief executive on Thursday, ending a tenure that turned a maker of video-game chips into the engine of the artificial intelligence boom. The decision followed revelations of an affair with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy, and allegations of a second relationship, with an executive who reports to him.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The turmoil is a Silicon Valley story with a significant Israeli subplot. Nvidia employs roughly 6,000 people in Israel, including on 18 floors of office space in a Tel Aviv skyscraper. Israel is home to the company’s largest R&D hub outside of the U.S. As well, Huang has been the driving force behind a plan to build a giant new campus in the country’s north. Huang has courted Israel for years, and the open question now is what happens to that commitment without him.

The Nvidia logo on facade of a skyscraper in Tel Aviv. Photo by Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images

Nvidia’s Israeli business traces back to 2019, when it agreed to buy Mellanox, an Israeli chip company, for $6.9 billion. Mellanox made the technology that lets thousands of chips in a data center work together as one machine. That technology is now central to how AI data centers are built.

Huang kept Mellanox in Israel, along with its patents and its sales . The Israeli teams’ work is now woven into Nvidia’s newest products, and includes building a chip meant to rein in AI tools that act on their own.

In the second quarter of 2026 alone, Nvidia’s Israeli operation booked $17.5 billion in sales , nearly a fifth of the company’s worldwide revenue and more than four times the sales of Teva Pharmaceuticals, the multinational Israeli drugmaker. Analysts credit Nvidia with largely driving a 13% jump in Israeli tax revenue , and its workforce there has roughly doubled since Oct. 7, 2023.

Huang’s attachment to Israel is not purely commercial. On Oct. 7, Avinatan Or, a chip engineer at Nvidia’s Israeli operation, was captured at the Nova music festival along with his then-girlfriend, Noa Argamani, in a video seen around the world. She was rescued eight months later. Or remained a hostage for 738 days.

Nvidia colleagues held vigils with his mother , Ditza, and Huang stayed in touch with the family throughout. When Or was freed in Oct. 2025, Huang wrote to employees that “Avinatan has come home.” Huang later hosted Or and Argamani at the company’s headquarters in California. This March, as the war with Iran broke out, Huang told Israeli employees that he was “ very worried ” about them.

Avinatan Or, a former hostage freed from captivity in Gaza, attends a homecoming celebration on October 21, 2025. Photo by Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images

Huang has called Israel a “ second home ” for Nvidia.

That attachment is intended to last. In December, Nvidia announced plans for a campus in Kiryat Tivon, near Haifa, reportedly second in size only to its Silicon Valley headquarters. Construction is set to begin next year, and the offices are expected to open by 2031, with room for up to 10,000 employees.

The next CEO has become a question in Israel, too. Kress, 59, has been Nvidia’s finance chief since 2013. The board says it will look both inside and outside the company for a permanent chief executive.

Haaretz speculated Thursday that two Israeli executives could be potential candidates. Both men studied at the Technion in Haifa. Michael Kagan, who was born in St. Petersburg, Russia and moved to Israel with his family after high school, co-founded Mellanox in 1999 and has been Nvidia’s chief technology officer for six years. items.summary_ko: Nvidia를 33년간 이끌어 온 공동창업자 Jensen Huang이 목요일 CEO에서 사임했다. 미국 정보당국이 중국 간첩으로 의심하는 여성 사업가와의 관계와, 자신에게 보고하는 임원과의 두 번째 관계 의혹이 사임 배경이다. 이사회가 후임을 찾는 동안 CFO Colette Kress가 임시 CEO를 맡는다.
items.content_ko: Jensen Huang은 Nvidia의 공동창업자로 33년간 회사를 이끌었으며, 게임용 칩 회사를 AI 붐의 중심으로 키웠다. 그는 미국 정보당국이 중국 간첩으로 의심하는 여성 사업가와 관계를 가졌다는 사실이 드러난 뒤 사임했으며, 자신에게 보고하는 임원과의 관계 의혹도 제기됐다. CFO Colette Kress가 이사회의 후임 선정 전까지 임시 CEO를 맡는다. 기사는 이스라엘과 관련된 부분을 강조한다. Nvidia는 이스라엘에 약 6,000명을 고용하고 있으며, 텔아비브 고층빌딩 18개 층을 사용한다. 이스라엘은 미국 밖에서 가장 큰 R&D 거점이다. Huang은 이스라엘 북부에 대규모 신규 캠퍼스를 짓는 계획을 추진해 왔으나, 그가 떠난 뒤 이 약속이 어떻게 될지는 불확실하다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.title: 미갤에 퀄리티 좋은 암호 퍼즐 올라왔는데 같이 풀어볼 사람?
items.content:
해킹 문제를 해결하는 Capture The Flag(CTF)을 다루는 갤러리입니다.

items.title: The anti-marketing aspect of the Gemini network
items.summary: web
items.content:
The anti-marketing aspect of the Gemini network

I like Gemini. Not the Google Chatbot but the network that existed before Google named its product. If you are enough of a geek, you may want to give it a try.

Creating a Blog in Gemini:// (brennan.day)

Eoin is counting the number of "capsules" on the Gemini network. A capsule is the equivalent of a "website" on the Web or a "hole" on Gopher. It’s a personal space, a bunch of pages. Blogs become "gemlogs".

Eoin’s first observation is that the number of active capsules is slowly growing. The network is healthy.

But his second observation is really interesting: there’s absolutely no correlation between the number of new capsules in a given month and articles about the Gemini protocol being promoted on the first page of Hacker News.

This is a confirmation of what I’ve benn trying to explain for years: your metrics and web statistics are completely useless. The number of visitors, the number of clicks are worthless if you are not a marketer trying to extract money from a big brand. They don’t mean anything.

By the way: you should really avoid Hacker News these days. The front page is heavily manipulated to promote pro-AI stuff and bury everything that might question wether fascism-capitalism is good.

Why is Hacker News like that? (drewdevault.com)

A Mozilla employee is leaving after 15 years and comes to a similar conclusion. Mozilla is awesome because it has always been abnormal. It is mostly used by abnormal people. This means that hiring "normal managers" who try to make it "normal" and chase "normal" metrics is, of course, a recipe for failure.

jr conlin's ink stained banana (blog.unitedheroes.net)

I always failed to understand those marketing people who try to be "like others but a bit cheaper". While all the value is being different enough to nurture your own niche.

I completely removed statistics from my blog in 2013. At the time, I had a very strong realisation that the blog posts that mattered most, those I was proudest of, and those that prompted people to mail me even years later all had mediocre statistics.

How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Web (ploum.net)

On the contrary, most of my hit, my "buzz", were quickly forgotten. But, being addicted to statistics, I was unconsciously adapting my writing style to improve those numbers. I was scrolling through social media posts that were highly popular while trying to create some myself.

Closing my social media accounts and, instead, procrastinating on Gemini had the opposite effect: making me read other ideas without caring about reactions, about popularity. Jsreed5 made the same observation while he was trying the Nostr protocol. While Nostr’s technicalities may be interesting by themselves, the content on it is similar to the one found of mainstream social networks. And our smolnet Gemini-formatted brains cannot take it anymore!

A Geminaut's View of Nostr (jsreed5.org)

We really need a simple Gemini hosting provider that would also provide a Web version, to welcome less technical-minded people who still may want to access a quieter, non-commercial, out-of-time virtual space.

Lot of people are trying Gemini and find that there’s no content on it, that they can’t have their news and dopamine hit on it. Well, that’s exactly the point.

There Is No Content on Gemini (ploum.net)

The fact that only a niche minority want to use it is also part of the point. Gemini might no be for you. That’s fine. The modern Web and even the real world (where every device is actively working against me and every human interaction seems to be about AI) is increasingly not for me. So let me have my strange niche space.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
items.content:
Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at “ intelligent eyewear ” for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy.

These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.

Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.

Google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. That will also determine the final pricing. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses.

The setup here is similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses we’ve seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. The experience should be similar to using Gemini Live on your phone, but it will be a lot easier to fire up the AI. You can say “Hey Gemini” or tap a touch-sensitive area of the frame to start interacting with the robot.

Since this is the same chatbot that operates across the Google ecosystem, it has access to your data and preferences. You can ask questions and get personalized answers, have Google Maps guide you by voice, or just talk with the AI to kill time. The glasses use custom open-ear speakers to limit distractions for those around you. Google notes the directional microphones should not pick up speech from other people, either.

Adding the camera feed is where things get interesting. When the AI can see what you see, it has the potential to do more work on your behalf. Google suggests asking Gemini for recommendations when looking at a bookshelf or glancing at an event poster to have the AI add it to your calendar. The glasses will also support Gemini Guided Vision, which provides conversational audio descriptions for people who are visually impaired.

The utility of these devices hinges on Gemini. I would be remiss not to point out that Gemini, like all AI systems, is not infallible. In fact, it can be frustratingly fallible at times. The chatbot still regularly screws up simple things like adding calendar appointments or identifying objects in an image in my testing, and when you don’t have a screen to verify the AI’s output, it may be harder to trust it. These devices will really only make sense if you can rely on Gemini to do things right, and that’s still not a guarantee.

All the Gemini-powered glasses from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker feature a 12 MP wide-angle camera capable of shooting photos and video. Google says it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure people don’t do creepy things with its intelligent eyewear, and that it doesn’t do creepy things to you—Google claims its approach respects privacy on “both sides of the lens.”

items.content_ko: 스마트글라스는 불편함과 개인정보 문제 때문에 수용에 어려움을 겪어 왔다. items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-126365 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to @astrojs/prism 4.1.2, and from @astrojs/markdoc 0.3.0 until 2.1.2, runHighlighterWithAstro() returned code unchanged when Prism had no grammar for the requested language, and callers inserted that result as raw HTML. A code block labeled with an unsupported language could therefore render embedded HTML and script instead of displaying it as text. The Prism component was affected when applications supplied untrusted code with an unsupported or attacker-controlled lang, and the @astrojs/markdoc prism() extension was affected for less-trusted content authors even when Markdoc's ordinary HTML rendering was disabled. items.summary_ko: Astro의 @astrojs/prism 4.1.2 이전 버전과 @astrojs/markdoc 0.3.0~2.1.2 버전에서 취약점(CVE-2026-126365)이 발견됐다. 지원되지 않는 언어로 표시된 코드 블록이 텍스트가 아닌 HTML과 스크립트로 렌더링될 수 있다. @astrojs/prism 4.1.2와 @astrojs/markdoc 2.1.2에서 수정됐다.
items.content_ko: Astro는 콘텐츠 중심 웹사이트를 위한 웹 프레임워크다. @astrojs/prism 4.1.2 이전 버전과 @astrojs/markdoc 0.3.0부터 2.1.2 이전 버전까지에서 runHighlighterWithAstro()는 Prism이 요청된 언어의 문법(grammar)을 갖고 있지 않으면 코드를 변경 없이 반환했다. 호출하는 쪽은 이 결과를 그대로 원시 HTML로 삽입했다. 그 결과 지원되지 않는 언어로 표시된 코드 블록에 포함된 HTML과 스크립트가 텍스트로 표시되지 않고 렌더링될 수 있었다. Prism 컴포넌트는 신뢰할 수 없는 코드를 지원되지 않거나 공격자가 지정한 lang과 함께 제공하는 애플리케이션에서 영향을 받았다. @astrojs/markdoc의 prism() 확장은 Markdoc의 일반 HTML 렌더링이 꺼져 있어도 신뢰도가 낮은 콘텐츠 작성자에게 영향을 줄 수 있었다. 수정 버전은 @astrojs/prism 4.1.2와 @astrojs/markdoc 2.1.2다. items.title: Why writing correct software is hard and why math (alone) won’t help us (2016)
items.content:
I was very happy to speak at Curry On once again. Last year, following our work with Quasar, I spoke on continuations vs. monads . This year I gave a talk about computational complexity results in software verification, a subject I became interested in while formally specifying and verifying our upcoming revamped version of Galaxy.

What follows is an extended version of the talk (embedded above), containing some additional proofs and results I didn’t have time to cover, complete with footnotes, for those wishing to study the topics further. Reading time: ~45 mins.

In this article, we try to understand the relationship between programs and correctness, and in particular, why writing correct programs is hard. We will review results from computability theory and complexity theory, and see that programs and complete understanding – which is required for correctness – are fundamentally at odds. The main contribution of this text is aggregating in one place some results (as well as some references) pertaining to the essential difficulty of producing correct software. My motivation was various statements I found online (such as this , although it is far from the only one) claiming that software correctness is easy to achieve with the right tools. While some tools may (and do) certainly assist ensuring programs are correct, correctness comes at a significant cost. The cost of correctness – like the energy cost of reducing entropy – is a result of the “natural laws” of computation, that cannot possibly be avoided.

The story of theoretical CS began about a hundred years ago. With the growing success of mathematical logic, the mathematician David Hilbert laid out a program to formalize all of mathematics. He wanted to prove the formalism consistent and complete, and to find a decision procedure, an algorithm for determining the truth of every formal statement:

Consistency : proof that no contradiction can be obtained in the formalism.

Completeness : all true mathematical statements can be proved in the formalism.

Decidability : an algorithm deciding whether any statement is a theorem ( Entscheidungsproblem )

Hilbert believed that anything that can be formally reasoned can also be fully understood, and by that I mean all of its properties proven.

the 19th century view on the limits of knowledge was expressed by the maxim “ignoramus et ignorabimus”, meaning “we do not know and we will not know”. For his retirement in 1930, Hilbert gave a lecture – “Naturerkennen und Logik” (Logic and the understanding of nature) – in Königsberg to the Society of German Scientists and Physicians which he challenged this view. He said:

For the mathematician there is no Ignorabimus, and, in my opinion, not at all for natural science either. … The true reason why [no one] has succeeded in finding an unsolvable problem is, in my opinion, that there is no unsolvable problem. In contrast to the foolish Ignorabimus, our credo avers: We must know, we shall know! 1

Those words – Wir müssen wissen. Wir werden wissen – are inscribed on his tombstone.

Unbeknownst to Hilbert at the time, his program had been demolished a day earlier, when Kurt Gödel tentatively announced his first incompleteness result 2 .

Gödel’s incompleteness theorems demolished the first two pillars of Hilbert’s program ( some say also the third, only he didn’t realize it 3 ), and in 1936, Church and Turing broke the third, that of the decision problem, with proofs of what is today known as the halting theorem.

The halting theorem – CS’s first theorem – was proven in both Alonzo Church’s 4 and Alan Turing’s 5 papers in 1936. The theorem is so fundamental to the essence of computation that it is no accident that it appeared alongside both formulations of computation. It states that there cannot exist an algorithm that decides whether any given program ever terminates. Baochip-1x: A Mostly-Open, 22nm SoC for High Assurance Applications (bunniestudios.com)

An MMU (memory management unit, allows for hardware support of virtual memory, a feature normally reserved for "real" computers)

items.summary_ko: Baochip-1x는 bunnie가 만든 22nm 칩으로, MMU와 TRNG, AES 등 보안 기능을 갖추고 있다. 적외선 카메라로 칩 구조를 직접 확인할 수 있도록 설계됐다. Rust로 작성된 마이크로커널 OS인 Xous를 실행하기 위해 만들어졌다.
items.content_ko: Baochip은 bunnie가 내놓은 최신 오픈·신뢰 가능 하드웨어 프로젝트다. Baochip-1x는 22nm 공정의 SoC(시스템온칩)로, 가상 메모리를 하드웨어로 지원하는 MMU를 갖췄다. 또한 TRNG(진정 난수 생성기), AES 암호화, 다수의 암호 해시 등 보안 기능을 하드웨어로 지원한다. 저렴한 적외선 카메라로 칩 구조를 직접 확인할 수 있도록 의도적으로 검사 가능하게 설계됐다. 이 칩은 bunnie의 Precursor 기기를 위해 처음 만들어진 Rust 마이크로커널 OS인 Xous를 실행하도록 제작됐다. Xous 0.10.0에서 Baochip-1x 지원이 추가됐다. 글쓴이는 bunnie를 존경하며 RISC-V를 플랫폼으로서 흥미롭게 보고 있어 이 글을 쓴다고 밝혔다.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Libreboot 26.11 Released with Full UEFI Support, Drops GRUB Payload
items.content:
Libreboot , the free and open-source boot firmware project that replaces proprietary BIOS and UEFI firmware on supported hardware, has released version 26.11, transitioning to full UEFI support through the MrChromebox EDK2 payload, which also makes it compatible with Microsoft Windows.

With this release, nearly all supported boards now ship exclusively with EDK2 firmware. The project removed GRUB as a coreboot payload, along with the previously included MemTest86plus and CSMWrap payloads, simplifying firmware configuration and reducing maintenance.

However, this change comes with an important warning for existing users. Systems configured to boot in legacy BIOS mode must be migrated to UEFI, including setting up a proper EFI System Partition, before installing the new firmware. Otherwise, existing operating system installations may no longer boot.

Legacy booting is still possible, but users must add the required components themselves when compiling Libreboot. The build system now supports inserting GRUB EFI, MemTest86plus, and ReBIOS through its efi/ directory.

On the hardware side, Libreboot 26.11 enables TPM 2.0 by default on several systems, including the ThinkPad X270, X280, T480, T480s, and T580, along with the Supermicro X11SSH-F and Topton X2E N150. TPM support was previously disabled due to problems with SeaBIOS, which no longer occur with EDK2.

Dell Latitude laptops also receive fixes for fan control, battery status reporting, and lid-switch handling during suspend. These improvements use an updated ACPI implementation replacing older SMM-based patches. Furthermore, SD card reader functionality has been restored on the ThinkPad W541 and Dell Latitude E7240 through an EDK2 patch.

For Chromebook users, the release restores configurations matching upstream MrChromebox after changes in Libreboot 26.10 caused boot failures on some systems. The Dell OptiPlex 780 also switches to EDK2, while the OptiPlex 5050 SFF gains SATA hotplug support and a fix for PCIe error reporting related to certain wireless cards.

A security-related EDK2 fix addresses an ICMP packet bounds-checking vulnerability in its PXE implementation. According to the developers, Libreboot was not affected because its configurations use iPXE instead, but the patch has been incorporated into the distributed source code.

Finally, the release simplifies several aspects of Libreboot’s build system, including firmware payload configuration, source handling, and ROM naming. Custom firmware images now use clearer BIOS and UEFI prefixes. Improvements to the lbmk build utility make it easier to insert additional EFI payloads and work with older firmware images.

For more information, see the release announcement .

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-126364 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpoint compared the requested local-image path with the build output directory without preserving case on case-sensitive filesystems. A sibling directory whose path differed from the output directory only by letter case could therefore pass the containment check, allowing an unauthenticated requester to read image files accepted by the image service from outside the output directory. Exploitation required on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a preexisting case-variant sibling directory; ordinary traversal to unrelated paths was already rejected. This issue is fixed in Astro version 7.4.7. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-12T22:33:17.635Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-126364

items.content_ko: Astro는 콘텐츠 중심 웹사이트를 위한 웹 프레임워크다. 5.14.3부터 7.4.7 이전 버전까지 Astro의 /_image 엔드포인트는 요청된 로컬 이미지 경로를 대소문자를 구분하는 파일시스템에서 출력 디렉터리와 비교할 때 대소문자를 보존하지 않았다. 이 때문에 출력 디렉터리와 대소문자만 다른 형제 디렉터리가 포함 여부 검사를 통과할 수 있었고, 인증되지 않은 요청자가 이미지 서비스가 허용한 이미지 파일을 출력 디렉터리 밖에서 읽을 수 있었다. 공격 조건은 @astrojs/node 어댑터를 사용한 온디맨드 렌더링, 대소문자 구분 파일시스템, 미리 존재하는 대소문자 변형 형제 디렉터리다. 관련 없는 경로로의 일반적인 경로 순회(traversal)는 이미 차단되어 있었다. 이 문제는 Astro 7.4.7에서 수정됐다. 게시일은 2026-11-12이다.

Update: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO at 9:00 AM ET . The company's CFO, Colette Kress, is the interim CEO.

The Jensen Huang scandal is one of the most remarkable tech stories in recent memory, and, in my view, it’s less about the now ex-Nvidia CEO’s alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy than the tsunami-grade ripple effects of one man’s questionable choices.

We do not know, nor do we have proof, that Jensen Huang's (whose departure was confirmed by Nvidia on Thursday morning) alleged relationship with Alice Huang resulted in any kind of quid pro quo, or in state or industry secrets being leaked or traded. Even so, Huang is surely smart enough to know the perception: the incredible irresponsibility of an extramarital affair, allegedly with a woman who, even if she isn’t a spy, is an influential businesswoman in China, the biggest economic and strategic rival to the United States.

(Image credit: IOT Analytics ) Nvidia chips are, according to a 2025 report by IOT Analytics , in 92% of all Data Centers. Ironically, virtually every AI-generated meme currently doing the rounds featuring Jensen Huang and Alice Huang (they’re not related) — and there are hundreds of them — has probably been generated using Nvidia hardware.

Nvidia is a publicly traded company, and its fortunes impact global markets — and right now everyone is nervous. Jensen Huang’s actions are the latest PR disaster for an industry that’s already struggling with major trust issues . Many people already worry that AI is not being developed or employed in our best interests, and that the companies creating these foundational models are chasing money, rather than dreams of heroic medical breakthroughs, climate change solutions, and occasionally finding previously unseen Mayan ruins . (I think they may be doing all of the above, but that’s just me.)

I get it if you think that one person's infidelity can't possibly have any bearing on an entire tech industry. I disagree. Huang’s fortunes are inextricably tied to those of AI. There might not be an AI industry without Nvidia and Huang (again, see Nvidia's AI market share numbers above), and so you have to question what the future of the industry looks like without his specific vision for AI hardware over the next few years.

This is about much more than the fact that Jensen Huang had an affair. It's about who he had the affair with, when it happened, what information might have been shared, and how, if any of this is true, Jensen Huang might have been used to steer US chip policy in relation to AI, and reshape the global AI race to favor or assist China. The fallout from all that boggles the mind — and it may reshape our AI future.

items.title: Nintendo Takes Down Emulators and Firmware in Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep
items.content:
Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.

This isn't the first time Nintendo has sent takedown notices to GitHub, and it's not even the first time it's tried to take down Yuzu , but the focus this time around seems to be on firmware for mod chips. This particular firmware had 144 repositories, all of which have been removed by GitHub and replaced by a DMCA takedown notice. Mod chips like Picofly can be soldered onto the Nintendo Switch's mainboard, and can be flashed with this firmware to circumvent Nintendo's copy protection.

GitHub has posted Nintendo's November 6 DMCA notice , which says, "The Nintendo Switch console and video games contain technological protection measures ('TPMs') that permit the Nintendo Switch console to interact only with legitimate Nintendo video game files. This process protects Nintendo’s copyright-protected video games, (...) by preventing users from playing pirated copies of Nintendo’s video games on the Nintendo Switch console and by preventing users from unlawfully copying and playing Nintendo’s video games on unauthorized devices."

However, while this takedown has effectively wiped out a ton of repositories with mod chip firmware, it seems like it's still being hosted elsewhere on the site, according to TorrentFreak . It's possible, though, that Nintendo isn't finished yet; back in 2024, Nintendo effectively took down 8,500 copies of Yuzu by issuing a takedown that targeted 12 different mirrors of the emulator.

This particular takedown also comes a few days after emulators were able to run the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on PC, so this could be a sign that Nintendo is winding up its lawyers to crack down on emulation once again.

If anything, emulation is a completely different beast in 2026 than it was even in 2024, thanks to the rise of AI. There's already been a wave of AI-made mashup mods that took over Twitter for a couple of weeks, and led Anthropic to coding in a lock to prevent Claude from outright copying games . Game developers have started cracking down on AI ports of games, too. Just last month Rockstar had to take down a browser version of GTA 5 , and Bethesda took down an AI-generated Fallout New York game .

items.content_ko: 닌텐도는 GitHub에 DMCA 삭제 요청 네 건을 보냈다. 대상은 Switch 에뮬레이터 Yuzu와 Citron Neo, 그리고 모드칩 펌웨어다. 기사에 따르면 닌텐도가 GitHub에 요청을 보낸 것은 이번이 처음이 아니며, Yuzu를 노린 것도 처음이 아니다. 다만 이번에는 모드칩 펌웨어에 초점이 맞춰진 것으로 보인다. 이 펌웨어 저장소는 144개였고 모두 GitHub에서 삭제되어 DMCA 삭제 안내로 대체되었다. GitHub는 닌텐도가 11월 6일자로 보낸 DMCA 요청 원문을 공개했다. 요청서는 Switch 콘솔과 게임에 TPM이 있어 정품 닌텐도 게임 파일과만 상호작용하며, 이 조치가 해적판 게임 실행과 무단 복제를 막는다고 주장한다. 입력 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

using GNU binutils's strings will detect these paths, right?

The answer is no , at least when using GCC and targeting x86-64 : you should not assume that string constants end up literally in the binary.

In this C++ source we create a std::string from a string constant:

Compile with GCC 12 or later and run, which prints the path:

But the path occurs precisely 0 times in the binary itself:

Surely these bytes must be part of the binary somewhere ? Let's run strings on it and grep just for the /home prefix:

with a made-up subdirectory xbrew ? How?

The answer is that GCC optimizes our std::string{PREFIX} . The fact that we see something that looks like the prefix is merely a coincidence.

GCC splits our string up into two (overlapping) pieces of 16 bytes, like so

which fit exactly in xmm registers, so that it can copy our string to the std::string buffer using vectorized move instructions.

Filtering the relevant bits from g++ -O2 -S -masm=intel , we get

and our string is stored at .LC0 and .LC1 as constants, which just happen to be next to each other in the binary:

In general, this happens when a string constant is copied into a buffer, as with std::string , strcpy or memcpy ; strings that are only passed around as pointers, like in fopen(PREFIX "/x", "r") , stay intact.

Some package managers like Conda and Spack install packages into a padded prefix during their builds, with the idea that they can be “relocated” to a shorter prefix of the user's choice: the binaries are patched in-place. Conda uses a repeated string _placehold in a directory name to make the prefix long enough.

Now, even if we pick a 256-byte path (a convenient multiple of all x86-64 register widths) by padding the path Conda-style

and keep our fingers crossed that GCC puts the pieces of the path contiguously in the binary, we do not see our prefix back in the binary. What we get instead is a much shorter string of only 176 bytes (that is 11 times 16):

This is thanks to a further optimization: since the string _placehold repeats every 10 bytes, the 16-byte pieces repeat every lcm(10, 16) = 80 bytes, and GCC needs to store only 5 distinct 16-byte constants for the padding:

For string literals, I don't think so. Clang does not split strings into constants, yet it generates essentially the same instructions. For example, take a longer path, and target AVX2 with -march=x86-64-v3 :

Clang simply puts the string in a section dedicated to strings, .rodata.str1.1 :

and copies its 53 bytes with two overlapping 32-byte ymm loads and stores, at offsets 21 and 0:

That isn't particularly different from GCC's version, which loads the same two pieces from constants in .rodata.cst32 instead:

So what does GCC gain? In terms of performance, probably nothing measurable: both do the same loads and stores. With repeated pieces, GCC might have a slight edge, because a repeated piece is loaded once and stored multiple times (11 loads for 16 stores in the earlier example). It also uses aligned reads, but that matters only for ancient CPUs.

In terms of size, GCC's pieces can take more space than the string itself: overlapping bytes are stored twice, and the pieces are aligned to 16, 32 or 64 bytes. The 53-byte path above takes 64 bytes as two pieces, against 54 bytes as a string. It only pays off if it results in deduplication, for example when many strings share a prefix of at least 16 bytes for SSE2, 32 bytes for AVX2, and 64 bytes for AVX-512. Presumably deduplication does not save much in practice, especially now that some distributions use AVX2 as their baseline.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Jensen Huang To Step Down As Nvidia CEO Amid Affair Scandal
items.content:
Nov 12 (Reuters) - Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

Huang’s exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia, one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump .

Huang also had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has learned. Reuters is not naming the woman, and attempts to reach her were not successful. Nvidia declined to comment.

The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration’s oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment.

Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick’s future. Earlier, a White House official said US President Donald Trump “maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position.”

Huang’s departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia’s shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly $6 trillion.

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang records a pool interview on Thursday Sept. 17, 2026. (Jonathan Brady/PA via AP, Pool, File) via Associated Press

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang’s departure.

While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia’s reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products.

Nvidia shares were down 5.5%at $164.22, paring earlier losses. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares heavily on Thursday as the price fell, showing the AI trade is very much alive. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6% each.

Huang, Nvidia’s fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61% stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair.

“The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period,” Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on November 18.

Kress was gathering Nvidia’s executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving.

Huang hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. Paul Weiss did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

items.title: SmartTube LOCAL: piss off Youtube with a local account, subs and offline playback
items.content:
SmartTube LOCAL is an independent fork of SmartTube , built for people who want the convenience of YouTube, the freedom of their own video archive, and a little more control over what appears on the family TV.

YouTube is great. Google... not so much.

SmartTube LOCAL takes the excellent SmartTube Android TV app and pulls an additional rabbit out of its ass: use your own OFFLINE YouTube video library, right alongside ONLINE YouTube, WITHOUT a Google account.

Download videos with MeTube or yt-dlp, save them to a network share, and watch them on your TV. No internet required after that. No Google account required either.

Or watch YouTube online without a Google account, block ads and sponsors, subscribe to channels, and save playlists locally.

By your powers combined! You are Captain Youtube!

YouTube and your downloaded videos, all in one place. Browse, search, subscribe, create playlists, block ads and sponsors, and watch your own videos.

Browse your downloaded videos by channel, search your archive, open playlists, and watch everything directly from your home network.

YouTube can enshittify all it wants. You can just sit there and lol at it.

Want the kids to ONLY have access to your downloaded video archive?

Me too. That's why (in part) this exists.

Create separate profiles for the family, each with their own subscriptions and playlists.

Set their profiles to LOCAL ONLY , choose which channels or videos they can access, and protect the settings with a master password.

Now the kids can watch what you've downloaded, without an accidental detour into the brainrot side of YouTube.

Everybody shares the same video archive, so there's no need for multiple copies of anything. Each profile just sees what you've allowed.

Can I bring my YouTube playlists and channels with me?

Of course you can. What do you think I am - a hack?

Already have a carefully curated collection of playlists and enough subscriptions to last several lifetimes?

Import your playlists from Google Takeout and your subscriptions from NewPipe-compatible JSON.

There is no catch. You don't even have to star this repo.

I just got big mad about needing to provide photo ID to Google to watch frikken YouTube, so I decided to do something about it.

Then I decided to do a bit more. And a bit more.

Not much. You just need to apply a soupçon of elbow grease.

Technically, you need an SMB network share for your downloaded videos. That could be a NAS, Raspberry Pi, a USB drive plugged into your router, or even a broken $20 laptop.

This repository is maintained offline for private use, but I push updates here as a backup, and for your entertainment.

Also, because I don't want to punch holes in my firewall just to install this thing on every relatives TV.

So please, feel free to use it. In fact, host as much of your own shit as you can.

PS: No support or compatibility guarantee is provided.

PPS: Pull requests are not accepted at this time.

PPPS: Please DO fork and fiddle with this to your heart's content.

PPPPS: As this is a vital piece of personal infrastructure (I have two kids, and SmartTube LOCAL is needed to maintain my sanity), I intend to maintain it. That may mean the project goes in directions that don't suit your needs.

To that end, I'm publishing the current 32.71 source code and final release , with the source code frozen at this version.

Download the APKs from the SmartTube LOCAL GitHub Releases page .

I'll continue to publish updated APKs as I hatch them.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-126362 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. Request-controlled slot names containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Svelte component using a client:* directive and dynamic rendering of the attacker-chosen slot; components that did not render that slot emitted only Astro's escaped fallback content. Both server rendering and client-side hydration used the unsafe slot name.
